subdomain: 3.8 Evaluate progressive discovery vs. monolithic context strategy

en.question: A Claude Messages API 2023-06-01 application uses tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119 on a supported model. Every task uses one compact case-status tool, but only a few of the other authorized specialist tools. Loading the full catalog consumes substantial initial model context. Which configuration best balances discovery overhead and context use?

options.text: Defer the case-status tool as well as every specialist tool so all tasks begin with the same discovery step.
options.note: This can reduce upfront definitions but imposes search latency for an operation every task needs. Keeping the compact common operation available directly avoids that unnecessary step.

options.text: Leave every definition loaded and rely on prompt caching to remove unused definitions from the context window.
options.note: Caching reuses prefix processing but does not remove tokens from model context. It does not provide the relevance selection needed for the large, mostly unused catalog.

options.text: Set defer_loading on the search tool itself so no tool definitions enter initial context.
options.note: The documented search tool must remain non-deferred so the model has a way to discover other tools. Deferring the discovery entry point breaks that configuration.

options.text: Keep search and the common case-status tool non-deferred, and defer the authorized specialist definitions.
options.note: The common operation remains immediately callable while rare definitions enter model context only when discovered. Deferral changes loading strategy, not the application's authorization obligations.
